name: India
intro: It's August 1947. You are free at midnight — and split in two at the same instant. Trains arrive full of the dead. Kashmir is already in dispute. You have 340 million people, almost no industry, and a leader, Nehru, who thinks the world is about to divide into two armed camps and India should join neither. Both camps will try to buy you. Choose what "non-aligned" means when the bills come due.

nodes.title: Midnight and Kashmir
nodes.situation: Partition violence kills up to a million. Pakistani tribal fighters invade Kashmir; the Maharaja accedes to India. Nehru wants a UN plebiscite; Patel wants the army to finish it.

choices.label: Take Kashmir to the UN, Accept a Ceasefire…
choices.summary: Take Kashmir to the UN, Accept a Ceasefire Line

effects.text: The 1949 ceasefire line becomes the Line of Control
effects.insight: a frozen war for 75 years

effects.text: India learns the UN is a great-power tool; its faith in international law is bruised
effects.insight: A choice in one capital changes the options available elsewhere. Local leaders respond to the new balance of risk and opportunity.

effects.text: Pakistan's identity forms around the Kashmir wound
effects.insight: the army becomes the state

effects.text: Both offer to mediate; both are refused
effects.insight: non-alignment's first act

effects.text: Refugee resettlement succeeds better than anyone expected
effects.insight: the state's first competence test.

choices.label: Push the Army to the Border
choices.summary: Push the Army to the Border — Take All of Kashmir

effects.text: Full Indian control by 1949; a permanent Muslim insurgency
effects.insight: Kashmir as Ireland

effects.text: Pakistan turns to the US in 1948, not 1954
effects.insight: SEATO/CENTO early; the US–Pakistan military alliance is deeper

effects.text: A second India–Pakistan war in 1950
effects.insight: A military commitment consumes resources and creates new security fears beyond the original battlefield.

effects.text: Britain, still refereeing the Commonwealth, sides with Pakistan
effects.insight: India considers leaving

effects.text: China, watching, revises its own Himalayan claims
effects.insight: the 1962 war may come as 1955.

choices.label: Accept Partition of Kashmir Along Religious Lines Now
choices.summary: Accept Partition of Kashmir Along Religious Lines Now

effects.text: The Valley goes to Pakistan, Jammu and Ladakh to India; a settled border by 1950
effects.insight: Nehru is called a traitor

effects.text: No Kashmir obsession; Pakistan's army is smaller, democracy stronger
effects.insight: maybe

effects.text: Hindu nationalists gain; Gandhi's assassination (Jan 1948) is followed by riots
effects.insight: A choice in one capital changes the options available elsewhere. Local leaders respond to the new balance of risk and opportunity.

effects.text: The US rewards the settlement with aid; India is a Cold War prize
effects.insight: Economic dependence gives the country supplying money, fuel or trade political leverage.

effects.text: East Pakistan, watching the West get Kashmir, feels ignored
effects.insight: the 1971 split comes early.

nodes.title: Panchsheel
nodes.situation: Korea is at war; the US wants a vote against China; China has occupied Tibet. Nehru drafts "Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence" with Zhou Enlai. The US offers Pakistan a military alliance.

nodes.title: Suez and Budapest
nodes.situation: Britain invades Egypt; the USSR crushes Hungary. The West asks why you condemn Suez loudly and Hungary softly. Krishna Menon at the UN abstains on Hungary.

choices.label: Condemn Suez Hard, Hungary Softly
choices.summary: Condemn Suez Hard, Hungary Softly

effects.text: Nasser becomes your closest partner
effects.insight: the NAM's Nehru–Nasser–Tito triad

effects.text: Tito, who faced the same choice, shares your dilemma

nodes.title: The Himalayan Shock
nodes.situation: Your Forward Policy has pushed posts into disputed territory; China has warned. Your army is unprepared; Defense Minister Menon says China won't attack. The generals say it will. Cuba is in crisis; nobody is watching.

choices.label: Forward Policy, Get Defeated, Ask the West for…
choices.summary: Forward Policy, Get Defeated, Ask the West for Arms

effects.text: The army collapses in a month; China withdraws voluntarily
effects.insight: humiliation without conquest

effects.text: Nehru is broken and dies in 1964; India doubles its army and starts a bomb program
effects.insight: A threat to one side changes the other side’s calculations, encouraging it to build or seek protection.

effects.text: Kennedy airlifts arms; Pakistan, furious, turns to China
effects.insight: the Sino-Pak axis is born

effects.text: Khrushchev, busy with Cuba, backs China
effects.insight: then reverses; India's Soviet tilt deepens after

effects.text: Ayub Khan concludes India is weak
effects.insight: the 1965 war is planned here.

choices.label: Pull Back the Posts, Negotiate a Swap (Aksai…
choices.summary: Pull Back the Posts, Negotiate a Swap (Aksai Chin ↔ Arunachal)

effects.text: No war; a settled border; Nehru is denounced as an appeaser at home
effects.insight: A military commitment consumes resources and creates new security fears beyond the original battlefield.

effects.text: Zhou's offer (real, 1960) is accepted
effects.insight: China and India are the Asian pillars of the NAM

effects.text: Pakistan, denied a Chinese ally, is contained
effects.insight: Partners judge a commitment by what it costs you to keep it. A changed commitment reshapes their choices.

effects.text: India needs no US arms; non-alignment survives intact
effects.insight: A choice in one capital changes the options available elsewhere. Local leaders respond to the new balance of risk and opportunity.

effects.text: Nehru's Congress loses seats in 1962 but he lives to 1964 in better health
effects.insight: his successor is not chosen in panic.

choices.label: Prepare Properly
choices.summary: Prepare Properly — Delay the Forward Policy, Build the Army First

effects.text: The war comes in 1964 instead and is a stalemate
effects.insight: no rout, no shock

effects.text: A stronger India means China negotiates
effects.insight: or makes the Sino-Pak pact earlier

effects.text: US arms come before the war, not after
effects.insight: India is closer to the West already

effects.text: Khrushchev sells MiGs in 1962
effects.insight: India's Soviet arms dependency starts the same, for different reasons

effects.text: Menon is fired before, not after
effects.insight: the civil-military rift heals.

nodes.title: Tashkent
nodes.situation: Pakistan infiltrates Kashmir (Operation Gibraltar); you counterattack toward Lahore. The US cuts arms to both; the USSR offers to mediate at Tashkent. Shastri must decide what to accept. Famine looms; the US ties food aid to policy.

choices.label: Accept the Tashkent Ceasefire, Return Captured Ground
choices.summary: Accept the Tashkent Ceasefire, Return Captured Ground

effects.text: Shastri dies the night after signing; Indira Gandhi becomes PM
effects.insight: a dynasty by accident

effects.text: The USSR is now the subcontinent's referee
effects.insight: the US is out

effects.text: Johnson's "ship-to-mouth" food aid humiliates India; the Green Revolution is born from that humiliation
effects.insight: Economic dependence gives the country supplying money, fuel or trade political leverage.

effects.text: The war changes nothing on the map
effects.insight: Pakistan's army learns nothing

effects.text: East Pakistan, undefended in the war, realizes the West won't protect it
effects.insight: 1971's seed.

choices.label: Reject Tashkent
choices.summary: Reject Tashkent — Keep Haji Pir and the Lahore Approaches

nodes.title: Bangladesh and the Bomb
nodes.situation: Pakistan's army is massacring Bengalis in the East; 10 million refugees have crossed into India. Nixon is backing Pakistan (it's his China go-between). You've signed a treaty with Moscow. Your scientists can test a bomb.

choices.label: Sign With Moscow, Liberate Bangladesh, Test the "Peaceful"…
choices.summary: Sign With Moscow, Liberate Bangladesh, Test the "Peaceful" Bomb in 1974

effects.text: A 13-day war; 93,000 Pakistani POWs; Bangladesh is born
effects.insight: India's greatest strategic victory

effects.text: Nixon sends the USS Enterprise; a Soviet fleet shadows it
effects.insight: the closest India came to a superpower war

effects.text: "Smiling Buddha," May 1974
effects.insight: Pakistan's Bhutto vows to "eat grass" for a bomb; he gets one

effects.text: Nixon and Kissinger's tilt to Pakistan is remembered in India for 40 years; the US–India relationship stays cold until 2005
effects.insight: A choice in one capital changes the options available elsewhere. Local leaders respond to the new balance of risk and opportunity.

effects.text: China, the intended audience for 1974, accelerates aid to Pakistan's nuclear program.
effects.insight: Economic dependence gives the country supplying money, fuel or trade political leverage.

choices.label: Liberate Bangladesh, Skip the Bomb
choices.summary: Liberate Bangladesh, Skip the Bomb

effects.text: No test; Pakistan's program has no trigger
effects.insight: maybe

effects.text: Carter later rewards India with nuclear cooperation; the 2005 deal happens in 1978
effects.insight: A threat to one side changes the other side’s calculations, encouraging it to build or seek protection.

effects.text: Bhutto still pursues a bomb (he decided in 1965) but with less urgency and funding
effects.insight: Economic dependence gives the country supplying money, fuel or trade political leverage.

effects.text: China's aid to Pakistan is slower
effects.insight: Economic dependence gives the country supplying money, fuel or trade political leverage.

effects.text: Indira's popularity is slightly lower without "Smiling Buddha"
effects.insight: the Emergency of 1975 may still come.

choices.label: Stop at Refugee Relief
choices.summary: Stop at Refugee Relief — No War, No Treaty

effects.text: The genocide continues; a longer guerrilla war; Bangladesh independent by 1975 with a million more dead
effects.insight: A military commitment consumes resources and creates new security fears beyond the original battlefield.

effects.text: 10 million refugees stay; West Bengal's politics collapse into violence
effects.insight: A choice in one capital changes the options available elsewhere. Local leaders respond to the new balance of risk and opportunity.

effects.text: Nixon is pleased; US aid to India rises
effects.insight: the "tilt" pays

effects.text: The USSR courts Pakistan instead
effects.insight: its 1970s South Asia policy flips

effects.text: Indira is attacked as weak; her authoritarian turn comes sooner.
effects.insight: A choice in one capital changes the options available elsewhere. Local leaders respond to the new balance of risk and opportunity.

nodes.title: The Reckoning
nodes.situation: Rajiv Gandhi's army is bogged down in Sri Lanka. Kashmir is erupting. The USSR — your patron, your arms supplier, your trade partner — is dissolving. Foreign reserves cover two weeks of imports. Manmohan Singh, the new finance minister, proposes tearing up the License Raj.

choices.label: Withdraw From Sri Lanka, Liberalize the Economy in…
choices.summary: Withdraw From Sri Lanka, Liberalize the Economy in 1991

effects.text: The 1991 reforms: tariffs cut, licenses abolished
effects.insight: 300 million exit poverty over 25 years

effects.text: The IPKF leaves; the Tamil Tigers assassinate Rajiv in 1991
effects.insight: A choice in one capital changes the options available elsewhere. Local leaders respond to the new balance of risk and opportunity.

effects.text: The insurgency explodes; 40,000 die over two decades
effects.insight: A choice in one capital changes the options available elsewhere. Local leaders respond to the new balance of risk and opportunity.

effects.text: The USSR is gone; India's arms and oil lines are cut
effects.insight: it turns to Israel, then the US

effects.text: A slow thaw; the 1998 nuclear tests interrupt it; the 2005 nuclear deal completes it.
effects.insight: A threat to one side changes the other side’s calculations, encouraging it to build or seek protection.

choices.label: Stay in Sri Lanka, Protect the License Raj
choices.summary: Stay in Sri Lanka, Protect the License Raj

effects.text: A Vietnam-scale quagmire; India's army bleeds for a decade
effects.insight: A military commitment consumes resources and creates new security fears beyond the original battlefield.

effects.text: IMF bailout with harsher terms; reforms come anyway, in 1994, with less choice
effects.insight: Foreign decisions alter domestic coalitions. Leaders must answer to the institutions and people keeping them in power.

effects.text: The rupee-ruble trade's collapse is catastrophic
effects.insight: Economic dependence gives the country supplying money, fuel or trade political leverage.

effects.text: With the army in Sri Lanka, Kashmir is worse
